description: Of 31,062 homicide victims in Mexico in 2023 (INEGI preliminary), 27,221 were men and 3,578 women - 87.6% against 11.5%, with 263 unspecified.
energy_note: Twenty-seven thousand men, in one year.

description: A study of INEGI mortality data covering 605,260 homicides from 1990 to 2022 found 538,996 - 89.05% - were male. The age-adjusted rate for men in 2022 was 41.55 per 100,000 against 5.48 for women.
energy_note: Half a million men, over three decades.

description: In firearm mortality analysis, one third of victims were aged 20-29, though rates among children and adolescents rose at a faster proportional pace.
energy_note: A third of them in their twenties.

aspect: EXAMPLE - Mexico's male share exceeds the world's
description: UNODC's 2023 Global Study on Homicide found 81% of homicide victims worldwide were men in 2021. Mexico runs several points above that.
energy_note: Even by world standards, unusually male.

aspect: Where it happens differs by sex, which matters
description: Nearly one in five female homicides occur in the home, against one in thirteen for male homicides. Male killing tracks organised crime; female killing has a weaker relationship to it and more often involves intimate partners. These are two different problems with one statistic.
energy_note: He dies in the street, she dies in the house.
notes: Recorded deliberately so this dataset cannot be read as diminishing femicide. Different mechanisms, both real.

description: INEGI builds from death certificates via the mortality registry, capturing homicides never formally investigated, which is why its count exceeds SESNSP's every year. Two official numbers exist and they do not agree.
Male life expectancy in Mexico stalled and reversed during the peak violence years - an effect large enough to move a national demographic indicator, which is rare outside war.
energy_note: Enough killing to shorten the national lifespan.

aspect: Every man in the family has a story
description: At these rates the violence is not statistical for anyone - a cousin, a neighbour, a schoolfriend - so the fear is memory rather than anticipation.
energy_note: Not afraid of what might happen. Remembering.
